reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Gullible Carpenter and its frame at the end of The Snake in the Prince's Belly; the frame is stated correctly: the owl counsellor Red-Eye tells it to the owl counsellors before King Foe-Crusher.

Age band 16+ (adult relationships, told non-explicitly): the lover only arrives and comes near her, and his compliance with the 'goddess's' remedy is one non-explicit line; the remedy is shortened to calling another man home and embracing him. Ryder's slur for the wife is removed. Each change and every omitted line is disclosed.

The infidelity is clear to adults from the night invitation, the bolted door and the remedy; the content note states it plainly in both languages, with the husband's passing thought of killing both, which he never acts on.

The comic core survives: 'do not touch me', the invented warning in the goddess's name, 'ಭೇಷ್, ಪತಿವ್ರತೆ!', thanking the lover for a hundred years, and carrying both on his shoulders to the relatives' doors. No em dashes; the pause question comes before the reveal.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, 315 KB; one generation with uneven rows, re-gridded by uniform scaling and cropping as the credit states; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text.
The carpenter, the wife and the guest are consistent and fully clothed in every panel, with similar skin tones and no caste markers (the wife's bindi is not one).

The cot is empty and made in every interior panel; nobody touches anybody in panels 3 and 4. Panel 5 shows him lifting his wife onto his shoulder; panel 6 the comic night procession with laughing relatives. Nothing is suggestive.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children or parents.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.

Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol (gpt-6.1-sol is not available to this account) and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
